item.title: An in-depth report into the structure of the Foundation.
item.description: A tale idea which will take the style of a report explaining the the highest levels of the SCP Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: Factual, Informative

Page Layout: Report title and brief summary of purpose, note from report's author, tier explanation, 05 council, ethics committee, administrator, general high level staff

Elevator Pitch: A report commissioned by the 05 council simplifying and explaining how the different branches of the SCP Foundation interact and their relevant powers and duties. The report will contain an explanation of the 05 council, the ethics committee, the administrator and all their associated staff as well as my own idea for classifying the different levels of authority in the Foundation (this system is currently only planned to be used within the context of the report).

Central Narrative: A factual report written by a high level member of staff under the orders of the 05 council.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Provides an understanding of several mysterious and poorly understood groups and individuals.

Additional Notes: This information varies between cannons so I will only be able to apply my own personal interpretation. I already have notes on paper but I do not want to commit to a draft until I hear some early feedback from the community.

item.title: @fterlife.net (seeking greenlights)
item.description: An online database website that contain the soul of every deceased human.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights: Yes
Page type: SCP article
Page layout: standard layout
Object class: Eculid
Containment proceduce: Any attempt to access SCP XXXX online must be redirected. The main focus of containment is to conceal the existence of this database from other group of interests. Testing required level 2 or higher.
Description: An online database. When an X digits number is inputted, it might allows the user to enter a page with documents about a deceased person and an AI resembling that person. At the moment, the foundation has only gained access to a small amount of pages. Others are locked and require "Administrator's permission".
Addeum: Through some of the accessable page, the foundation manage to explore the afterlife (resembling fhe afterlife in Divine Comedy but some element are more related to technology and simulation).
Hook: The main idea of this article is that since we spend so much time on the internet, it is slowingly become similar to a religion. Furthermore, I believe the exploration logs will be really interesting as messing around in hell using codes are as fun as it sound. I also want to link this to Mekhane, perhaps by using the internet so much, we sunconciously repair a part of his heart: his dream.

item.title: Gun-thers Armory
item.description: Hehe Anomalous Guns Go Brrr
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Fairly heavy test log.

Elevator Pitch: A gun store named ‘Gun-thers Armory’. It has all the amenities you would expect (Firing Room, Break Room, etc). It is open at almost all hours, closing at 23:30 on Saturday, and reopening at 0:00 on Sunday. Every time the store is reopened, there will be 1 firearm inside a glass case that is anomalous. The glass case will not restock until the store closes and reopens. It also has some other minor anomalous properties, but they seem to minor to list.

Central Narrative: The foundation investigates the store under the guise of “Safety Inspectors”. They investigate the place’s 1 worker who works there for the entire time (anomalously severe case of insomnia lets him work all week.). The guy believes all of the weaponry is non-anomalous and considers it as irrelevant to talk about his job, so the foundation just puts a mic on their glasses to monitor them. As for the store itself, the foundation try to make the minor anomalies seem normal to the public, and just buy the anomalous gun the second the store opens. Other than that, it’s just testing the weaponry out in test logs.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: MTFs are allowed to use any weapons created, excluding those deemed unsafe for usage by the ethics committee, those ineffective for what the foundation requires from their weaponry, or those who have too minor an effect to replace standard issue weaponry.

item.title: Pranking Mimic
item.description: A safe SCP that loves pranks.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy/Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • Mimics dangerous SCP/animals/objects to scare.
  • It is a notorious prankster
  • Has light memetic properties that make those around it believe.
  • Once a fear based response is obverse, the SCP cannot help but laugh.
  • Safe
  • Would have octopi like ability to change shape and texture of body to resemble other creatures. Use color shifting ability to induce memetic effect.

Central Narrative: Foundation following up about a creature terrorizing a small city, find this SCP. After the initial violent encounter, which injuries the creature. After containment, it is shown to be friendly albeit mischievous. It often escapes containment, regardless of how secure, and pranks staff on site mainly by scaring them.

Two directions of narrative:

  1. It accidentally kills an older staff member by scaring them.Tries to urgently revive them.It shows regrets and becomes more docile. However, it is now shown on occasions to mimic that staff member on site and interact with others without suspicious. This brings up the question how long it was able to do that.
  2. A peculiar cruel guard that has shown on number of occasions to beat the SCP after being scared. Shows up dead in his home after the SCP was found missing for a day.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A safe killable SCP with possible hidden agenda.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) What Lurks in the Shadows
item.description: A First SCP about anomalous shadows.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Elevator Pitch: A phenomena in North-Western Nevada that manifests in the form of shadows. These shadows form in place of normal shadows, but once manifesting, can only be removed if a deer heart is cast into it. When any mammalian matter, live or dead, passes into the shadow, it is devoured at a rapid rate by numerous small, unseen entities. If this occurs, and a deer heart is not fed to the shadow within 5 minutes, the instance will spontaneously grow to a much larger size until it is fed a deer heart.

Central Narrative: First began occurring in the Massacre Rim Dark Sky Sanctuary, Nevada, before spreading to the nearby 100 kilometres, including a Foundation site. The deer heart protocol was discovered when a deer ran into an instance and it disappeared. The Foundation then discovers that during a solar eclipse, the into 100 kilometre area will become one massive instance, killling everyone inside. A final addendum implied that its area of influence is growing.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Focusses on the very common fear of the dark and what may lurk inside. Furthermore, there is the implication that it is growing, and a solar eclipse may one day threaten an end of the world scenario.

Additional Notes: It is inspred by the Aztec Goddess Itzpapalotl, so there are reasons behind the deer heart and the solar eclipse.

item.title: Indignant Fuel
item.description: The soul of a Daevite king is slowly drained from the crown it resides in and used as a source of electricity, much to the king's indignity.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Light comedy

Page Layout: A normal SCP page with copies of the original SCP pages for both the crown and the machine converting it into power, and logs of the Daevite king's increasingly desperate threats and pleads.

Elevator Pitch: A potentially world-ending, keter-class malevolent spirit is put into a device from the factory that slowly burns it up for power, which the spirit takes very personally.

Central Narrative: A keter-class Daevite crown is haunted by the spirit of the king that wore it in life, and repeatedly attempts containment breaches, each with greater success than the last, and the SCP staff in dread of its eventual escape. The situation is inverted when the crown is successfully cross-tested with a machine from the factory which converts souls into electrical power, and the test is made a permanent part of both SCPs' containment, reclassifying them as a single SCP. The spirit of the king threatens, then bargains, and finally pleads to be released from the device, but is ignored and slowly fades away.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The humiliation of a potentially world-ending SCP.

Additional Notes: Whether or not I can use occupied SCP numbers for the archived articles of the two SCPs that were combined, and help not messing on the Daevite and Factory lore.

item.title: The Unneeded Pact of Fire
item.description: Civilian interference causes a Safe-class SCP in Alaska to change to Keter-class.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The main meat of the SCP would be mainly within a journal written by SCP-XXXX-01

Elevator Pitch: This SCP consists of 3 entities: SCP-XXXX would be a chiminea outside a town in Alaska that can only be lit with human remains. SCP-XXXX-01 would be tied to the chiminea and lure people into lighting a fire in the pot and adding their bodies as fuel. If the fire is not lit for a set amount of time, SCP-XXXX-02 will appear out of the nearest lit flame and drag the closest human into the flame, resetting the clock.

Central Narrative: The bulk of the article would be in the form of a journal written by SCP-XXXX-01 revealing the history of SCP-XXXX and why the fire needs to be lit. The previously mentioned town was struggling during the first winter after settling, fires wouldn’t stay lit and people were freezing. A woman (SCP-XXXX-01) leaves to get supplies for the town, and when returning notices the SCP Foundation has descended on the settlement. She sees the Foundation as the “bad guys”, and eventually makes a deal with SCP-XXXX to allegedly get rid of the Foundation in the area and save her town and family from the harsh winter. This ties her to SCP-XXXX, and she is now charged with keeping the fire lit and SCP-XXXX-02 at bay.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP would have been a Safe classification if not for civilian interference. I think it would be interesting to explore the idea of an SCP realizing they have unwittingly doomed themselves and made matters worse trying to save others. SCP-XXXX-01 would watch and document her family moving on without her, and the town expand and advance to the point where a deal to save the town from a harsh winter isn’t needed anymore, but the deal remains.

Additional Notes: My one fear is not getting a good enough connection/back-and-forth between SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-01 to make the deal appealing enough to take, but that’s a bridge to cross in the draft stage. Also the title can use some critique as well.

item.title: Humanity, for Dummies
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
The Foundation doesn't normally treat SCP's compassionately or particularly humanely. But when a dangerous anomaly shows a sliver of humanity and has valuable people hostage, the Foundation has to rush to turn a monster into a caring person.

Central Narrative:
A dangerous anomaly launches an unexpected attack on a Foundation facility, injuring a number of key individuals including the Site Director. It is incapacitated when it falters in attacking a pregnant woman. The Foundation discovers that the anomaly may kill the injured individuals at any point via its anomalous effect. The anomaly decides that violence is not the best way to go about its goal and demands access to sensitive documents under threat of the death of its victims. The Foundation, citing its failure attack the pregnant woman, theorizes that the anomaly may have a slight compassion for humanity, and sets a psychiatrist/therapist on the case to attempt and bring that to the forefront.

Hook:
The main idea I want to run with is a normally callous Foundation having to do its absolute best to make an anomaly care about the people around it.

item.title: SCP Idea: “For Rosa”
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: A book that turns male humans into a copy of the author.

Central Narrative: The book is a copy of Capitalism and Freedom, written by Milton Friedman. The back of the cover has a written message on it that reads, “For Rosa.”

When a human male makes contact with the book, they will undergo a transformation period, eventually ending with them becoming a copy of Friedman. These copies retain all memories of Friedman’s life at the time he was 50 years old.

item.title: SCP idea: CODE NAME: T.T.P
item.description: Just an SCP idea. This SCP is in very very early development.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights: no

Page type: SCP concept

Elevator pitch:
SCP code name: T.T.P

T.T.P is a humanoid who is covered in long, thick, black hair, this hair seems to be unaffected by gravity.

T.T.P has a plush toy which it refuses to let go of, it is extremely protective of this plush toy.

T.T.P is extremely tall, around 9 feet tall.

T.T.P has large marble like green eyes which are incapable of blinking.

T.T.P will not physically harm anyone unless its plush toy is touched or it hears an extremely loud noise. If T.T.Ps toy is touched they will go into a fit of rage and brutally attack whoever touched it. If T.T.P hears an extremely loud noise it will be extr aggressive towards anyone it seems for the next 10 minutes. No one has ever been recorded to have survived one of T.T.Ps attacks.

T.T.P is childlike when it is not aggressive. When presented with toys it will normally begin to play with said toys. If given crayons they will begin to scribble on the walls. It seems to be very much entertained by such activities.

T.T.P sheds hair gradually over the course of months. shed hairs are quickly replaced by new hairs furthermore shed hairs continue to be unaffected by gravity. Direct physical exposure to a shed hair from T.T.P causes exposed subjects to experience terrifying hallucinations of T.T.P, subjects commonly have 5-6 hallucinations per day and normally never stop experiencing them, there seems to be no way to reverse the effects of exposure.

Direct physical contact with T.T.P causes the exposed subject to immediately become terrified of seemingly everything, the subject with normally kill themselves in the next few days. Yet again there seems to be no way to reverse the effects of exposure.

Central narrative:
T.T.P was discovered by accident while the INFORMATION CLASSIFIED was conducting a mission to plan a possible way to extract the Titanic from the Atlantic ocean. A submersible vehicle which has been given the name Seacat (which was being piloted by Cpt. Gala Smyth and copiloted by Dr. Thomas Snow) was using a device to digitally map out weak points in the sunken ship when an extremely odd shape was picked up within the ship.

Curious to discover what was being picked up by the device Cpt. Gala Smyth ejected a mini RC submersible from the Seacat. Dr. Thomas Snow then proceeded to steer the mini sub towards a small breach on the ship as to enter the vessel.

After a few minutes of searching different rooms Dr. Snow spotted something which made their stomach sink and their hair stand on end; a tall, black, linky figure stood motionless in the corner of a desolate room which was being poorly illuminated by the flash light on the mini sub.

Cpt. Smyth soon noticed Dr. Snow staring at the monitor with a horrified look on his face. She jokingly punched the doctors shoulder, asking him if he'd seen a ghost but the smile was soon ripped off her face as she turned her attention to the image on the monitor. Her jaw dropped. She stared at the figure, trying to make sense of it.

Cpt. Smyth soon swallowed her fear and regained her composure before shaking Dr. Snows shoulder and telling him to pilot the mini submersible out of the ship and back to the Seacat. Silently the doctor nodded his head and did as requested before Cpt. Smyth piloted her sub to the surface, shivering every now and then at the thought of the creature they had spotted.

The company was informed of their discovery and the SCP foundation was soon called in. The company was INFORMATION SECRET as to ensure that they kept quiet about the discovery.

Hook/attention grabber:
I think that my concept is fairly interesting due to the very odd looks of this SCP and the odd combination of childlike innocence and brutal aggression. I also think that the location in which this SCP was discovered is quite odd and allows people to speculate what it was doing there.

Additional notes: please keep in mind that this SCP is still in very early development and that this is also my first ever attempt at actually creating an SCP. I really want to know if this concept has potential and where or how it can be improved. If you really like this concept then I will continue to develop it and some day see if I can get it green lit, if you don't like it then I'll scrap it and start a different concept.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - The Tontine Tree
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I am seeking a greenlight for my SCP proposal.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout: SCP article in progress to allow the reader to see the Foundation's progression in understanding an SCP.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a tree. When touched by a living entity, a crude tattoo of an 'M' appears on its forehead, marking it as a contestant in a game. In addition, a portion of the contestant's lifespan will be taken away, physically aging the contestant. When there is only one living contestant left, they receive all of the life taken by the tree.

Central Narrative: The wizard who created the tree wants the process to end because he too is a player. Unfortunately, the Foundation discovers the tree at around this time.

When the Foundation discovers the tree, they observe only it ages living things that touch it and conclude that is the extent of its anomalous properties. However, the subjects that have touched the tree are kept on site to find any long term effects of exposure. When strange events occur on base, they are attributed to the tree but are actually the effect of the wizard breaking into the site and killing test subjects.

Following revisions will include further testing as a result of the new 'phenomenon'. A parallel effort is made to search the surrounding area for animals effected by the SCP to investigate long term effects of the SCP. However, when they find animals effected by the SCP are dying of natural causes AND the that they die only when being quarantined in the site, they suspect a third party.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A small Foundation facility tries to fix their flawed understanding of an SCP while being sabotaged by an unknown entity.

Additional Notes: 

The article can end two ways: the wizard is caught and a potentially humorous interview begins.
Alternatively, the Foundation can find concrete evidence the wizard exists but he remains at large.

Thank you for your time. I would appreciate any feedback you may have.

[Edit Jan 4, 2020 - Idea fleshed out, thanks to JamaisJ]

item.title: Seeking greenlight for my idea: The fibonacci watch
item.description: Revised idea of my original SCP idea. Seeking greenlights and feedback.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Page Layout: Standard layout, including a picture of the watch, interviews and testing.

Elevator Pitch: When wearing this watch, all sequences of numbers will become the Fibonacci code. All numbers change in the wearers eyes to be in the sequence of 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 and so on. The wearer will also only be able to complete mathematic equations including the Fibonacci code. Images or paintings including faces will also turn into the face of Fibonacci.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP will be revealed throughout a series of interviews and tests. The first interview is with the original owner of this SCP, now named SCP-XXXX-A. SCP-XXXX-A is a human male, approximately 1.7m in height. His personality is described as “Partially paranoid and curious.” During his interview, SCP-XXXX-A, who originally owned the watch before it was acquired by the foundation, will describe it as "A comfortable item of clothing I used to wear." They will state that after purchasing it from a local garage sale in █████, they did not notice anything strange until a few days after, when they wore it for the first time. They will say that numbers in their life started to change rapidly, and he could no longer do basic equations other than those in the Fibonacci code. He will then state that when visiting an art museum with his family while wearing the watch, all self-portraits and paintings including faces turned into the face of Fibonacci. He also noted that in real life, people's faces did not change to that of Fibonacci. Finally, the man will state that after 5 consecutive days of wearing the watch, he began to become terrified of the watches power and decided to call the police. The police did not care about the man's concerns as they did not believe him, but the foundation later contained SCP-XXXX-A and SCP-XXXX during a raid of SCP-XXXX-A's house.

The second section of narrative will be a series of tests performed by a Dr. █████. The first test will be a test to see if the SCP can make any form of image of a face transform into Fibonacci's. A D-Class personnel will be given 3 copies of the same image. One will be a digital .png file, one will be printed onto paper and one shall be an artist's renditioning of the image. After wearing the watch for 10 minutes with the images in front of them, the D-Class will then be asked if the faces in each image changed to that of Fibonacci. The D-Class will state that yes, all faces became Fibonacci’s. The second test was conducted on a D-Class that had previously been a mathematician before being contained at Site-██. This test included the D-Class wearing the watch while solving multiple simple equations. The first 12 equations that the D-Class solved were done with general ease, however, after this point, the D-Class seemed to struggle with solving further equations. When asked why, the D-Class simply stated, “It’s Fibonacci. It’s all Fibonacci.” The third and final test was conducted using SCP-5755 (http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-5755) A D-Class personnel was given 4 images while wearing SCP-XXXX, all the images being of SCP-5755's “sources”. The D-Class is then asked to say the numbers in the sources, and gives the output, “112358, 132134, 558914, 423337”. They are then asked to shuffle the papers and once again say the numbers in the sources. The D-Class only repeats the same numbers they originally stated. These are of course the beginning numbers of the Fibonacci code in sequential order, and not the correct source numbers.

Hook/Attention Grabber: It's a watch that tells time in Fibonacci code, displays numbers in the Fibonacci code and overall changes the wearers mind into that of a pure follower of Fibonacci and his sequence.

Additional Notes: This is a very detailed SCP, and I have done my best to include each detail that I would like to be put into the final article in this greenlighting pitch. All feedback is also welcome. Thanks!

THIS IS VERSION 2

item.title: Labeling an SCP and determining its Object Class
item.description: Trying to figure out the Object Class for an SCP that sorta contains more than one SCP. I don't really know how to explain it quickly.
item.content:encoded:
Just some notes before I get into it:
1. Not entirely sure I am putting this thread in the right place since I have never posted on here before. If it is in the wrong place, I am sorry and could you please direct me to the right place?
2. I am not looking for a critique on the SCP I am writing. It is extremely unlikely that I will ever post the page for the SCP because I have no confidence and I just like writing these for fun.

I have two questions I need answers and one may answer the other.
Here is the situation. What I am going to refer to as SCP-X is a large sphere-shaped object that can be used to open a dimensional portal. SCP-Y is a sentient being that has come through the portal from the other dimension. SCP-Y is the only known being that has crossed over. The Foundation does not know if there are more beings on the other side because the portal closed again before they could explore it, and they do not know how to reopen it. SCP-Y has no connection to SCP-X aside from coming through the portal opened up by SCP-X. With that in mind, would the two be kept in the same SCP entry?
If the answer is no, then ignore the rest of this. If the answer is yes, I have another question.
SCP-X is considered Safe. Just build a structure around it (since it is too big to move) and it won't do anything. SCP-Y is Euclid. It is a sentient and sapient being that needs the same basic needs as a human. It also does not like to be contained and may try and break out, but none of its abilities really make it any harder to contain than a normal human. If SCP-X and SCP-Y were to be under the same entry, what would the Object Class at the top of the entry be?

Thanks for any help.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Loneliest Goddess
item.description: There's a god or goddess for everything- how about a goddess of atheists?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch:

A goddess referring to itself as the Matrem Obliviscetur, or Forgotten Mother, who is the Goddess of Atheists. It derives its power from disbelief, so the fewer people who know of its existence, the more power it gains. However, it suffers from a paradox of belief: Because it is benevolent, it wishes to help atheists by answering their prayers. However, since atheists lack belief in gods, they never make requests. This has made it extremely powerful, but it has limited ways to exercise this, being resigned to giving its followers "gifts" of luck or small boons, which more often than not hurt the recipient more than help.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: A series of discovery logs tell the Foundation's unwitting discovery of the Matrem posing as human in order to be closer to its followers. A series of interviews with the Matrem by various researchers bring to light its origins and its clear depression. Subsequent experiments are conducted where it is encouraged to interact with several atheist D-class personnel, over the course of which its depression only worsens, and it is discovered that the Matrem's emotions affect a wide-ranging area, causing the inhabitants of nearby regions to become despondent. In order to prevent further damage, the Foundation provides a solution for the Matrem by which it is provided with subjects who are made aware of its existence and make a request of it, and then given amnestics in order to wipe their memories of the encounter, making them eligible to receive the aid.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of a god that exists for no reason, as a sort of reversal of the idea that life is meaningless and has no purpose, as experienced by an immortal whose very purpose cannot be fulfilled

item.title: Greenlight SCP - omniscient
item.description: What would happen if humans knew anything?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: Humans learn things throughout life. But, what if they born with all the knowledge?

Central Narrative: This scp is an eleven-year-old human boy who appears to know all the things in the universe. He can also tell the date and time of someone's birth, and the date, time, and how someone will die. At first, everyone thought he sees the future, but he denied it, and said he only knew.

He has big brown eyes and hair of the same color. According to research done, he looks like a normal boy from the inside out.

The organization managed to reach him through a call that the scp himself made. Follow the call below:

//SCP: Hi, am i talking to Dr. XXXXX of the SCP foundation?

Dr. XXXX: Yes …. Wait, how do you know that kind of information?

SCP: I know many things, come and get me, i am waiting.//

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A kid who knows everything.

Additional Notes: This scp refused to answer certain questions, such as "When will the world end?" or "Is there really a God?", or even the source of his knowledge. His statement was that answering these questions could put humanity at risk.

He knows how to do things like painting, cooking, playing instruments. He seems to have all the talents imaginable. Once he sang for a group of employees, everyone left delighted.

The organization tried to use him to acquire information from other scp's, but he refused to give it by saying that he should not interfere in this type of thing.

He can speak all languages, even the ones that aren't human.

He can walk freely around the organization.

He has already helped employees to repair machines and even communicated with scp's with different languages than a normal human.

He is not a affected by SCP-035, it looks like he can't be manipulated.

item.title: The Laughing Tree
item.description: A tree that convinces children to haze one of their own by tying him to its trunk. Any mention of this is brushed off with memetic laughter.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedure, description of the entity's feeding ritual, 2 interviews with a survivor of the ritual, and 1 interview with an involved camp staff-member.

Elevator Pitch: The Laughing Tree is a memetic entity rooted within an old wooden-tent campground commonly used by scouts or youth groups. The tree convinces children to tie one of their own to its trunk, upon which they are mentally scarred. Many of these children later runaway from home, but some of them return to the tree, carve their name in its trunk and kill themselves. Any mention of the tree, the tying, or the deaths are brushed off with casual laughter.

Central Narrative: A low-level foundation member calls attention to this entity after his child is almost tied to the tree. Previously, he laughed the tale off as a "camp story" to several co-workers. He is told to bring in his child for questioning.

+ show block
– hide block

The first interiew is short. After providing a cover story, the investigator asks what happened. Emotionally dead, the kid replies, "you'll just laugh at me.."

The second interview occurs after the parent tries to console their child. The parent tries to help answer preliminary questions by describing camp activities. At the mention of knot-tying, the child's face goes pale.

The interviewer asks why the child didn't want to attend camp. Instead of answering he makes a small digression about how he felt sorry for a spider that another kid burned. The parent interrupts and describes his child as socially isolated and wonders if this behavior is related to the nature of his work.

Eventually, the child describes what happened, One-by-one belongings of other scouts find their way to his tent. Camp staff approach him and ask about thefts. The child tries to explain that he didn't take them, but they laugh at him. He runs. Then they, the scouts, surround him with knot-tying ropes and force him toward the *tree*. He tries and fails to escape, as the scouts laugh at him. The laughter grows louder.. and deeper until he realizes that it's coming from behind. And then, the laughter stops.

The investigator asks what changed. The child looks down, and cries.

A third interview takes place with a camp staff-member and witness. He laughs at the hazing and the deaths, "Why should I feel sorry for a bunch of thieves?"

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Laughter, not as a coping mechanism but as something to be feared.

Additional Notes: Besides names, the tree also has "LOL" etched into its bark, and it is disgusted by urine.

item.title: The Memories of bygone age
item.description: A tree, impervious to physical damage
item.content:encoded:
A tree, impervious to physical damage that when touched briefly makes the person who touched it believe they are someone from the past.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type:** SCP Article:

Elevator Pitch: -Every time the tree is touched a different person from a random time period would be summoned to talk through an affected person.

-This appears to only be their memories

-This effect doesn't last very long, (about two hours), and the person is fine after this period.

-they just don't have any memory of when they were in that state.

-The tree itself is made out of materials that are unknown to anyone on Earth, and impossible to x-ray.

Page Layout: I would tell the story I have in mind through interviews and most of the interviews would be fairly normal.

Central Narrative: None of the people interviewed would have any knowledge of the tree. It would also become clear through the interviews that each random person was had lived fairly close to the location of the tree. The last log however would be different. It would be the king of a previously unknown civilization, and he would reveal that he was paranoid that his subjects were plotting to overthrow him and that a "man from the sky" had told him that he could help, as long as he let him study their culture. He would reveal that the tree was a listening device, that he was told could pick up and copy the memories of those around it, and store them, apparently indefinitely. The last thing the king would say was that the man needed to transport them all somewhere else for a while in order to study them, but that they would be back soon because the man needed to pick up his listening device.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I believe I can tell a story here that leaves a bit of mystery, while also leaving the potential for other stories to be told through the object.

Additional Notes:
So that's the idea, let me know if something like this has been done before, or if it's confusing in some way. Any criticism would be appreciated! Thanks.

item.title: A Blast From the Past
item.description: RIOT!!!!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Not Until Critique

Page Type: SCP Article,

Genre (Optional): Historical

Page Layout (Optional): Classic Article

Elevator Pitch: Many protests or gatherings are rather peaceful and have a lot of meaning, but what happens when they become more and more violent. Assault, looting, vandalism, streets being cut off, and people arming themselves. You will see it on the news as chaos in your city or somewhere else, but what if there is something else lurking in the streets and in the minds of those committing the violence that is out of there control, but forces them to think that's what they need to do.

The description of this SCP is a humanoid in the form of a male that manifests during times of major unrest. Contact with this SCP via abduction of individual(s), will cause that individual to become extremely violent towards property, law enforcement, and others in the opposition or pedestrians (reason on how it makes them extremely violent still being thought of). Once that one person becomes 'Corrupted' it may spread the violence to other people through mob mentality. The entity will continue to abduct more individuals when the violence peaks to make more people destroy and harm others while partaking in the violence itself as if it was one of the rioters.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The foundation has been tracking the entity for decades all around the world and containment is impossible, but to quell the violence is rather simple. Through agent emplacements and a protocol when dealing with a 'corrupted' individual (not yet thought of) The Foundation could prevent the spread. But the SCP foundation has no way to prevent all the violence as it may breach secrecy

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The foundation theorizes this entity has been around for centuries with possible manifestations during the Draft Riots of New York, the French Revolution, and farther back into recorded history. The entity as been dormant for over 20 years. First officially recorded during the Watts Riots.

Additional Notes: The way the corruption works is that the individual will think that they must start to destroy or harm the closest piece of property or even person. Other people will see this and start doing the same. The effect lasts for several hours until the SCP de-manifests then the effects will subside but the person will still think they did it as their own decision. The way Foundation agents can identify the infected individual

  • Foaming at the mouth
  • Extreme disregard for personal safety
  • Bloodshot eyes
  • extremely high heart rate and adrenaline

The Foundation knows what the entity looks like in a default state, but it will run away and blend into the crowds to hide.

item.content:encoded:
It's a doll-house replica of the abandoned house it is found in. Entering the room with the doll house causes you to enter the body of an out-of-place doll in the doll house…

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: It's a doll-house replica of the abandoned house it is found in. Entering the room with the doll house causes you to enter the body of an out-of-place doll in the doll house.

Central Narrative: The room is an old craft room. There are handmade dolls, but none of them look like the one subjects inhabit when they enter, which looks like a mass-manufactured doll. On the table the doll house sits on is a sign that says "Home Sweet Home", with a matching one on the wall of the doll's kitchen.

The bodies of subjects who enter the room through the door go limp and collapse to the floor (like a doll LOLOLOL), having fallen into a coma. Subjects awaken within the doll in the house. From inside, the house seems like a real house – the abandoned house, in fact, but in its heyday. It is populated by a family (the other dolls), who are warm and inviting. Subjects feel like they could live there forever (not anomalously so, but it would be a comfortable life). Those observing the doll house from the outside can see the dolls moving about as though manipulated by a child.

+ show block
– hide block

The only way a subject can stop possessing the doll is if another person enters the room through the door, whereupon they switch places; the first subject awakens from their coma and the other collapses.

Subjects trying to leave the doll house through the front or back door are met with gentle resistance from the other dolls. With enough insistence, the dolls will sadly allow the subject to walk out. Exiting puts them in a dark, hellish landscape topologically matching the abandoned home. The front door of the real-world home appears to them as a huge glowing portal. Upon walking through it, they disappear and the comatose body dies. Another completely different doll then immediately materializes in the doll house, inert.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This morphed from horror into something more wholesome in the process of conceiving it and honestly I think that became its strong suit.

Additional Notes: My knowledge of the catalog is far from comprehensive, so my main worry is that something that hits similar beats has already been done.

item.title: Halfway Found, Halfway Lost
item.content:encoded:
The following article is a sequel to SCP-5936, Critter Profile: Sparky! and SCP-5890. Whilst you can read it on its own, it's highly recommended you read all of the previous installments to get this article in its fullest.

item.title: I can feel its breath on my neck
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Classic SCP template with an interview log or two

Elevator Pitch: You know that feeling you get when you've got yourself good and spooked? That unshakeable certainty that something is behind you? You desperately want to turn around and prove yourself wrong, but at the same time you think that if you just keep looking forward and ignore the not-real thing behind you then maybe it'll go away. This SCP is the thing behind you, and it probably won't just go away.

Central Narrative: Mutiple potential directions for advancing the premise, feedback as to which sound more/less interesting is appreciated:

+ show block
– hide block
  • foundation investigations into the nature of the phenomenon. Is it an actual entity which stalks prey one at a time, or an infectious meme that inflicts a specific kind of terror in its host?
  • the progression of the 'infection', going from vague discomfort to all-consuming terror to actual physical harm
  • delving into the methods of transmission - I'm imaging a specific trigger phrase (such as the thread title) which causes the phenomenon to 'leap' from one victim to another. Of course, the fact that describing the symptoms infects the listener is a potential source of fun, both in an in-universe sense and in holding potential for fourth wall shenanigans (i.e. oh no you read the phrase in this article so when you get that feeling it's probably the real monster aaaaaa)
  • Alternative spin - there is no (known) trigger phrase or method of transmission, the phenomenon stalks a person until death and then attaches to another. Containment is based around tracking these people and preparing explanations/cover-ups for their imminent demises. Maybe its pattern of victims is revealing something? Maybe the last few have all been foundation personnel, and that suggests a bit more intelligence to the whole thing than makes us entirely comfortable?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The feeling of "there's something behind me I just know it" is more or less universal to anybody who has indulged in any kind of horror content ever. Hopefully this article can play off that shared feeling of dread.

Additional Notes: I'm not aware of a specific article but I admittedly wouldn't be shocked if the idea (or something very close) has been done already.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: INSTANT HOUSE - JUST ADD WATER!
item.description: A man who sells a product which, when touching water, instantly expands into a house.
item.content:encoded:
(this idea has been discontinued as it's too similar to SCP-1879)

Seeking Greenlights: No.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Comedy / Emotional.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article, with the bulk of it being inside of the Addendum - specifically, the backstory of the salesman.

Elevator Pitch: There's a man. The man has the classical personality of an overenthusiastic salesman. He offers to buy you an "instant house". It comes in a plastic packet. When the small object is mixed with a liquid that is at least 45% H2O then it will expand into a range of house sizes and qualities within 5 minutes. They also sell land for the house with it.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a man which is dressed in formal clothing, with a constant large smile. He sells houses, obviously. They're SCP-XXXX-1. There are numerous kinds of houses he sells - the price depends on how big and fancy. These are SCP-XXXX-1A through SCP-XXXX-1Z. He's capable of seemingly appearing anywhere / disappearing when no one is watching, however he usually appears to those without a home, or anyone who wants a new home. He accepts any form of currency, and packets are written in every language.
The main part of the narrative is the attempt to discover more about the SCP. 1: Where he gets these houses - as he's stated he does not make them, rather 'his company' makes them. 2: Where he's from, and how he gained the capability of seemingly just appearing and disappearing. 3: What he uses the money for. 4: Many other details about him.
Via addendum, this will be slowly but surely discovered. His reluctance to speak will make things much harder, along with his persistence on selling the house.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These 'homes' were created by the Group of Interest referred to as "The Factory". He is a salesman of The Factory, who offers this product to people in need of it. He was given the ability to 'appear' / 'disappear' anywhere via his clothing, also created by The Factory. It's seemingly melded into his skin, and become a part of him. The reason he's constantly so intent on working is because he, in fact, has a family which he needs to make money for. His large family required money which he struggles to make, so he's taken this job of selling instant houses for The Factory. The family's whereabouts are currently unknown.

Additional Notes: He'll have an advertisement which plays on TV, him starring in it. It'll be a pop-up on any website where the user is homeless, or unsatisfied with their home. Any device with an applicable user.

item.title: Looking for greenlight on my SCP idea
item.description: An SCP article about a mysterious communication station
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Mystery

Elevator Pitch: An SCP article about a mysterious communication station that receives broadcasts from the dead. After converting the data into audio, it can have uncanny effects on the listener.

Central Narrative: Appearing in no records and with no apparent purpose or owner, a comms station was secured by the SCP. The main tower doesn't receive standard electromagnetic transmissions, but nonsensical broadcasts from another realm. This data is harmless until converted into audio, where it can cause certain listeners to become obsessed with the sound, and most likely lead themselves to suicide. So what is the hidden power of the data, and why was the station built?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The transmissions the station receives cannot be located to any point in our universe. Its mysterious origins could explain why the audio drives only certain listeners to suicide.

Additional Notes:

After testing, which is described in the article, the Foundation theorize that the messages are the words of a deceased person. The comms tower can filter the broadcasts that will have an effect on the people in the area so that people will hear from someone they know such as a close friend or relative. If the person listens to audio from someone they don't know, they will be unaffected; but if it's from someone they love, they want to keep listening. If their feeling of regret is so strong, they might be tempted to take their own life to be with that person in an afterlife.

If people are interested, I can post my draft of the article.

item.title: Out of touch
item.description: You become desynchronized from reality.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes?

Page type: SCP article

Elevator pitch: An unknown anomaly avoids being seen or heard at all costs, and in doing so leaves everything in its wake in a state in which the effected persons are desynchronized from reality.
- This desynchronized state puts the person in a position where they cannot be affected by stimulus in the real world, and live life in a simulation created by their own consciousness.
- Their actions in this state are still carried out by their real life body, and do not match up with what is happening in the real world around them, often to the persons detriment.
- This state lasts a year.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Many small towns in eastern Europe have had large portions of their populations put into a catatonic state, with individuals suffering from this randomly moving limbs and speaking in one sided conversations. The foundation becomes involved and sends out an MTF squadron to locate whatever is causing this. The rest of the narrative of the article will follow the foundations vain attempts to stop the anomaly over the course of a year, juxtaposed with what the initial squadrons were perceiving as life. A key emotional theme of the article would be the loss of what you thought had been the best year of your life up to that point, and the mental toll that has.

Hook: Mainly the ideas of the challenging task of containing an anomaly while not being within several hundred meters of it, the unknown form of the anomaly itself and the varying accounts of afflicted individuals of the anomaly, and the terror of being restrained for a year without even knowing it.

Additional Notes: This is a rougher concept but I think it has potential. I want to try to workshop it into something that's up to foundation standards. Any and all feedback is appreciated.
